review_notes:
I reviewed all four declarations in ShellMixtures.lean (lines 1–69). I also read the definitions of `dyadicShell`, `shellEnergy` and `shell_energy_integrable` in Shells.lean, and the uses in FilteredClassShell.lean and TwoRootShellDecay.lean. In Mathlib I checked `charFun`, `charFun_eq_integral_innerProbChar` and their variable contexts, plus `BoundedContinuousFunction.integrable`, `integral_finsetSum_measure` and `integral_smul_nnreal_measure`.

`shellEnergy_weighted_sum_le` and `shellEnergy_weighted_sum_uniform` cannot be generalised beyond `Measure ℝ`, because `shellEnergy` itself is defined only for `Measure ℝ`.

In `shellEnergy_weighted_sum_uniform`, the hypothesis `hC : 0 ≤ C` is really needed. If `s` is empty, the left side is `shellEnergy 0 N = 0`, so `C < 0` would make the claim false.

The `hc : ∑ c ≤ 1` conditions are the natural sub-probability normalisation, so I did not flag them.

I could not compile the proposed generalisations. My claims that they go through rest on reading the instance requirements of the lemmas the proofs already use.

There is a near-duplicate copy of the first two lemmas in FalconerCompletion/Measures/AssemblyPositiveEnergy.lean. Since that is a duplication issue rather than over-specialisation, it is outside this rubric.

findings.excerpt: theorem norm_weighted_sum_sq_le {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℝ≥0) (z : ι → ℂ)
findings.problem: This Jensen/Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for sub-probability weights is stated only for complex numbers `z : ι → ℂ`. The proof never uses anything specific to ℂ. It uses only `norm_sum_le`, `norm_smul`, `Real.norm_eq_abs`, `Finset.sum_sq_le_sum_mul_sum_of_sq_le_mul` (which works on real numbers `(c i : ℝ)` and `‖z i‖`) and `pow_le_pow_left₀` with `norm_nonneg`. All of these hold in any real seminormed vector space.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalise the vector type:
`theorem norm_weighted_sum_sq_le {ι E : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℝ≥0) (z : ι → E) (hc : (∑ i ∈ s, (c i : ℝ)) ≤ 1) : ‖∑ i ∈ s, (c i : ℝ) • z i‖^2 ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, (c i : ℝ) * ‖z i‖^2`.
The proof can stay as it is. `norm_smul` turns `‖(c i : ℝ) • z i‖` into `‖(c i : ℝ)‖ * ‖z i‖` in any `NormedSpace ℝ E`, and the other steps are inequalities between real numbers. The edge case `s = ∅` is unchanged (both sides are 0). The caller at line 46 passes `charFun … r : ℂ`, so it still elaborates, using the instance `NormedSpace ℝ ℂ`.
findings.benefit: The same weighted-mixture bound then applies to characteristic functions with values in any normed space, to vector-valued Fourier transforms, or to plain real numbers. Users would not need to restate it. It would also remove the motivation for the near-identical `assembly_norm_weighted_sum_sq_le` copy elsewhere in the project.

findings.excerpt: (τ : ι → Measure ℝ) [∀ i, IsFiniteMeasure (τ i)] (r : ℝ) :
findings.problem: The statement that the characteristic function is linear in the measure, for finite non-negative combinations, is fixed to measures on ℝ. Mathlib defines `charFun` and `charFun_eq_integral_innerProbChar` for any `[SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]`. The integrability step uses `BoundedContinuousFunction.integrable`, which needs only `[OpensMeasurableSpace E]` and finiteness of the measure. `integral_finsetSum_measure` and `integral_smul_nnreal_measure` work for an arbitrary measurable space. Nothing in the proof uses ℝ. Mathlib also has no `charFun_add`/`charFun_sum`-style lemma, so this generalisation would fill a real gap.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalise to
`theorem charFun_weighted_sum {ι E : Type*} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [OpensMeasurableSpace E] (s : Finset ι) (c : ι → ℝ≥0) (τ : ι → Measure E) [∀ i, IsFiniteMeasure (τ i)] (t : E) : charFun (∑ i ∈ s, c i • τ i) t = ∑ i ∈ s, (c i : ℝ) • charFun (τ i) t`.
The proof can stay the same: rewrite with `charFun_eq_integral_innerProbChar`, apply `integral_finsetSum_measure` with integrability from `(BoundedContinuousFunction.innerProbChar t).integrable _`, then apply `integral_smul_nnreal_measure` to each term. Callers at line 45 and in FilteredClassShell.lean (`charFun_weighted_sum F (fun _ => (1:ℝ≥0)) τ r` with `τ : ι → Measure ℝ`) still elaborate, because ℝ provides all the required instances.
findings.benefit: The project is about planar Falconer problems, so measure mixtures on ℝ² or `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` are natural targets. A general version would give linearity of `charFun` over finite mixtures in every inner product space at no extra cost, and it would be a reusable lemma that is missing from Mathlib.
